Setting $\deriv{\mu}\ell = 0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0 &= \frac{1}{\sigma^2}\paren{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i - n\mu}
&& \text{(score for $\mu$)}\\
n\mu &= \sum_{i=1}^n x_i
&& \text{(multiply by $\sigma^2$; add $n\mu$)}\\
\mu &= \bar x
&& \text{(divide by $n$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

This solution does not depend on $\sigma^2$.
The second derivative is

$$\frac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \mu^2} = \deriv{\mu}\frac{1}{\sigma^2}\paren{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i - n\mu} = -\frac{n}{\sigma^2} < 0,$$

so for every fixed $\sigma^2$, $\ell$ is maximized over $\mu$ at $\bar x$,
and $\hat\mu_{\text{ML}} = \bar x$.
